name: Tennessee

administeringAgency.name: Bureau of Workers' Compensation
administeringAgency.parentAgency: Tennessee Department of Labor and Workforce Development

benefitCategories.medical: All reasonable and necessary treatment; Medical Treatment Guidelines apply; employer selects panel of 3 physicians
benefitCategories.temporaryTotal: 66 2/3% of wages up to max ($1,249.13/week 2024); max 450 weeks
benefitCategories.permanentPartial: Based on AMA Guides 6th Ed. impairment rating × multiplier (1-6×); varies by return-to-work status
benefitCategories.permanentTotal: 66 2/3% of wages; lifetime with scheduled cost-of-living adjustments
benefitCategories.deathBenefits: 66 2/3% of wages to dependents; max 400-450 weeks; $10,000 burial

workersCompensation.initialClaimForm: First Report of Work Injury (employer); Petition for Benefit Determination (employee)

appealLevels.name: Court of Workers' Compensation Claims
appealLevels.deadline: 1 year from injury or last payment

workersCompensation.enforcementPowers: Bureau compliance investigations; penalty assessment authority
workersCompensation.penalties: Penalties for uninsured employers; late payment penalties; civil penalties

programs.name: No State Disability Insurance
programs.note: Tennessee has no state temporary disability insurance program

programs.name: TennCare (Medicaid)
programs.eligibility: Low-income; Tennessee did not fully expand Medicaid (limited expansion proposals)

programs.name: Families First (TANF)
programs.eligibility: Low-income families with children; strict requirements

statutes.name: Tennessee Human Rights Act
statutes.protections: Disability discrimination for employers with 15+ employees; broader race/sex coverage at 8+

statutes.name: Public Protection Act (Whistleblower)
statutes.protections: Protection for refusing to participate in illegal activities or reporting violations

civilRightsFramework.retaliationProhibitions: Retaliation prohibited for filing complaints or participating in proceedings under THRA

accommodationObligations.standard: Reasonable accommodation for disability; follows ADA framework

laborStandards.agency: TN Dept. of Labor and Workforce Development
laborStandards.authority: Child labor; wage regulations (limited state minimum wage law)

occupationalSafety.authority: Tennessee Occupational Safety and Health Act; state plan state covering public and private

filingDeadlines.wcClaim: 1 year from injury date (strictly enforced under 2013 reforms)
filingDeadlines.civilRightsLawsuit: 1 year from THRC right-to-sue or 1 year from act if direct filing

dueProcess: Right to expedited hearing for medical necessity

evidentiaryStandards.wc: Preponderance of evidence; medical causation (more probable than not)

judicialReview.wc: CWCC → WCAB → Court of Appeals → Supreme Court
judicialReview.civilRights: THRC → Chancery/Circuit Court → Court of Appeals
judicialReview.eeoc: May dual-file with EEOC; federal court option

specialConsiderations.reform2013: Major 2013 reforms created new court system (CWCC), 1-year filing deadline, AMA Guides 6th Ed. requirement, and multiplier system for permanent partial benefits
specialConsiderations.amaGuidesRequired: Tennessee requires AMA Guides 6th Edition for impairment ratings—unique requirement
specialConsiderations.returnToWorkIncentive: Multiplier for PPD reduced if employer offers suitable employment; incentivizes return-to-work programs
specialConsiderations.toshaProgram: Tennessee is a state plan state with TOSHA covering both public and private employers
